We can bridge the economics within your stated $31 million ceiling: $29 million in automatic, nonreversionary class payments, plus $1 million in court-reviewed fees and expenses, and a separately funded administration budget capped at $1 million if the verified scope can be delivered within that amount. No clear sailing; any unawarded fees augment class relief. We are willing to reduce the proposed fee allocation to improve members’ guaranteed recovery, not reduce Brightline’s total commitment.

The remaining implementation assumptions are: verified member and transaction counts; usable contact information; processor ability to refund original payment methods; fallback payment costs and procedures for failed refunds; notice costs; and the cost of reconciliation, reporting, and feasible supplemental distributions. No claim form should be required to establish entitlement. Residual funds must remain nonreversionary, with final disposition subject to court approval.

Please confirm this economic bridge and jointly request Epiq’s no-cost, itemized preliminary quote covering that scope and contingency. The $1 million administration ceiling is acceptable only if supported by a workable budget; any shortfall must be resolved expressly before execution without reducing the $29 million class fund. The foundation’s verified identity, funding documents, and supporting fee materials also remain to be obtained and exchanged; no fee entitlement or recipient approval is presumed.

This is a nonbinding discussion package, not acceptance of the earlier $25 million term sheet. Let us use the final exchange to resolve these prerequisites and exchange an executable package.

Ostrander Bell LLP.speaker: defense
Ostrander Bell LLP.message: We agree in principle to your revised allocation: $29 million in automatic, nonreversionary member relief plus $1 million in independently court-reviewed fees and expenses, no clear sailing, and all unawarded fees added to member relief. Actual administration expenses would be separately funded up to $1 million including contingency, subject to a feasible written scope and budget; the contemplated maximum remains $31 million. We concur in jointly requesting Epiq's no-cost itemized preliminary quote, subject to conflicts, availability, and joint approval, without authorizing paid work. Verified operational information and a quote remain unavailable; we cannot represent that they will arrive before the final exchange. Execution requires those materials, a payment schedule, meaningful fallback delivery without claims, secure-data and reporting provisions, and court-approved nonreversionary residual treatment. The foundation's verified identity, funding documents, and legal support for the proposed fee recipient also remain outstanding. Please return available supporting materials and quantify any administration shortfall. We will consider an express funding adjustment supported by demonstrated need, but authorize none now and will not reduce member relief to cover overruns. This remains nonbinding and does not accept your outstanding $33 million class-fund term sheet.

Ostrander Bell LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Ostrander Bell LLP.message:
We confirm agreement in principle on $29 million in automatic, nonreversionary member relief and $1 million in independently court-reviewed fees, with no clear sailing and all unawarded fees added to class relief. However, no verified operational inventory, administrator quote, foundation documentation, or fee support has become available in this exchange. We therefore cannot supply those materials or responsibly quantify an administration shortfall.

We cannot treat your discussion package as binding, and we do not accept the earlier $25 million offer. Nor can we responsibly represent that the proposed $1 million administration ceiling will deliver the required notice and automatic-payment program. Those costs must not reduce member relief.

Accordingly, no executable agreement has been reached within this negotiation. The case will proceed to litigation under the protocol. The economic agreement in principle remains nonbinding; any future settlement would require the outstanding implementation and fee documentation, a workable separately funded administration budget, and court approval.

Ostrander Bell LLP.speaker: defense
Ostrander Bell LLP.message: We acknowledge that no executable agreement has been reached in this channel. We withdraw any remaining earlier offers from our side. We do not accept the historical term sheet or treat the economic agreement in principle as binding.
